title: Klaital's Shame
summary: A Stargazer tale about why the tribe buries its Rage.

claims.text: One Stargazer telling holds that Klaital did not try to halt an old massacre of humans but led it, striking first.
Ashamed afterward, Klaital washed in a river, walked away from the other Garou, and spent the rest of that life learning to hold Rage sealed inside.
Tellers say this is why Stargazers keep their anger buried and stand apart from other tribes, and they argue over whether that path is wise.

title: The Stargazers Go East
summary: The tribe's split from the Garou Nation in the modern nights.

claims.text: Many Stargazers have left the Garou Nation and now count themselves only among the Beast Courts of Asia, though a smaller number stay with Western packs and caerns.
The tribe was already few before many died at Shigalu; some believe only a couple hundred remain, and many have fallen to Harano.
Stargazers still call themselves a hopeful tribe, trusting that the Wheel turns and what dies is born again.
Most Stargazers are born in the East, and with breeding now centred there, more will be.

title: Songgao Mountain
summary: The site of the great Stargazer moot in China.

claims.text: China holds more Stargazers than any other land, some fled from Tibet and many born there among the Beast Courts.
Once a year, soon after the new year, the tribe meets atop Songgao Mountain to share legends and settle quarrels, usually by contests of complex games and only rarely by claw.
Other shapechangers and Garou of other tribes are not welcome at the gathering.

Legend says a rock there shaped like a sleeping dragon would split open to release an unmarked metis child if every living Stargazer gathered at once, and that metis would be healed of deformity from then on.
Chambers under the White Dragon Temple in Jiangsu are also dear to the tribe; a Stargazer from Dongting Lake is said to have taught the monks there a form of Tai Chi based on the wind.
